UNMATCHED_Battlegrounds_Mission.name: Battlegrounds Mission
UNMATCHED_Battlegrounds_Mission.text: Missions in Battlegrounds are weekly quests that include specific actions or objectives that the player can perform or achieve in order to receive rewards. In battlegrounds, rewards are given in XP, and serve as the primary mean of acquiring rewards on the Battlegrounds Track Missions can be viewed in the Battlegrounds menu, behind the "Season Rewards" tab. Contents Functionality 1.1 Gainging new missions List of missions Patch changes References Functionality edit edit source Observing the Missions in the Mission log Battlegrounds missions can be only completed in Battlegrounds. Players can only have 3 missions active at any time. Completing a mission will remove it from the list in the Mission log, making room for another. If a player has three missions and doesn't complete any of them (i.e. the mission log is completely filled), they will not receive new missions for the next week. Gainging new missions edit edit source Getting new missions Missions are awarded at 00:00, determined by region . This is often referred to as the "quest reset" or "reset time". The Americas region is set to PST; the Europe region set to CET; and the Asia region set to Hongkong/Taiwan time. Player reports suggest that the reset time changes to match daylight saving time during the summer months. There will be a countdown timer for the next quest to appear, which occupies the most-right empty slot. Once the reset time has passed, players with less than 3 missions become eligible to be awarded up to 3 new missions at the same time (depending on their amount of free slots), regardless of when players are in game or not. Progress cannot be made on such missions until they have been added to the quest log and revealed to the player. Therefore, players awaiting a new mission while in game menus are advised to log out and back in again after the reset time, in order to activate it before resuming play. Re-roll Players can choose to re-roll up to 1 mission each day by clicking the in the corner of its plaque in the Mission Log, immediately receiving a different, random mission in its place. If no is present in the Mission Log, re-rolls are not possible again until the next day. Any mission may be selected for re-rolling. All progress on a mission is erased when it is re-rolled; the next time the same mission is randomly assigned to the player, it will start with no progress. Limits While players may be assigned the same mission more than once over the course of their Hearthstone play, they will never be assigned a duplicate of a mission they are already on. Banking Missions can be banked for each Battlegrounds season. If a player misses a week, they can come back and complete that mission later. Battlegrounds Perks were optional perks that the player could purchase to improve their experience in Battlegrounds Battlegrounds Perks were removed in Patch 24.2.0.148211 and replaced with the Battlegrounds Season Pass Functionality edit edit source Battlegrounds Perks are optional perks that players can purchase to improve their experience in Battlegrounds. When Battlegrounds was officially released to the public on November 5, 2019, players could unlock Battlegrounds Perks by purchasing Descent of Dragons card packs. Players who had previously purchased Descent of Dragons card packs were also able to unlock these perks. 10 packs - Battlegrounds bonus stats unlocked 20 packs - Choose from 3 heroes, instead of the normal 2 30 packs - Visual emotes unlocked On March 26, 2020, a newly introduced Tavern Pass was made available for purchase for 2500 gold or $19.99 USD which provided an update to the existing Battlegrounds Perks, alongside 4 free Arena tickets. From March 26 to April 7, players who purchased the Tavern Pass replaced their old perks with these new perks instantly upon purchase. Upon the release of Ashes of Outland on April 7, all old perks expired. The new perks lasted for the duration of the Ashes of Outland expansion. Halfway into the expansion, the Tavern Pass went on sale for 50% off, costing 1250 gold in the in-game Shop and $9.99 USD on the online Battle.net shop Battlegrounds bonus stats Choose from 4 heroes, instead of the normal 2 Visual emotes Early access to new Battlegrounds heroes (normally 2 weeks until everyone has access) On August 6, 2020, the same Tavern Pass was made available for purchase again for 2500 gold or $19.99 USD, with the associated Battlegrounds Perks lasting for the duration of the Scholomance Academy expansion cycle. The Tavern Pass during the Scholomance Academy expansion cycle. UNMATCHED_Battlegrounds_Track.name: Battlegrounds Track
UNMATCHED_Battlegrounds_Track.text: Battlegrounds Track is a system in Battlegrounds that allows the player to earn various rewards in Battlegrounds by earning XP and leveling up. The Battlegrounds Track resets every Battlegrounds Season , typically in the X.2 patches The Battlegrounds Track was added in Patch 24.2.0.148211 , along with new Battlegrounds Missions and the Battlegrounds Season Pass associated with it. The Battlegrounds Track and Missions can be viewed by clicking on the "Season Rewards" icon in the Battlegrounds menu. Contents Battlegrounds XP Reward structure 2.1 Free rewards 2.2 Paid rewards and Season Pass 2.3 Season Pass+ Current season Patch changes References Battlegrounds XP edit edit source Battlegrounds XP icon Ways to earn XP, in-game tip Battlegrounds XP ) is an essential resource for leveling up in the Battlegrounds Track. Each level requires a pre-determined amount of XP to be reached. There are a total of 2 ways to earn Battlegrounds XP: Winning Battlegrounds games (top 4) Completing Battlegrounds Missions For more information, see Battlegrounds Mission Reward structure edit edit source Levels - Battlegrounds Track consists of 40 levels. Each level requires a certain amount of Battlegrounds XP, but also has an one-time reward for the player, as long as they reach that level. The Battlegrounds Track has two main reward types: Free Rewards and Paid Rewards . Both rewards use the same track. Functionality - The system will remark the reward with a blue glow to inform the player that it can be claimed. Then, the player needs to click or tap on it to confirm and claim it. If there is no blue glow, the player is still able to click or tap on it, but to view details of the reward. The system allows the player to view 4 levels at once and will mark the current level's range as default view. To navigate the adjacent sides of the Battlegrounds Track, the player can click on the arrow icons at the bottom of scene or swipe on mobile. Resets Next Season - The Battlegrounds Track refreshes the player's current progress after the next Battlegrounds Season is released. However, all the rewards will also be replaced with new ones, allowing the player to reach the levels again to get the new resources. All players will automatically be granted any unclaimed rewards in the old track if they have not done so. Free rewards edit edit source Free rewards are marked with a "FREE" text. The free rewards usually include Rare Emotes , Rare hero skins , Rare Strikes , and one Legendary hero skin. Paid rewards and Season Pass edit edit source Paid rewards are marked with a lock symbol. They are not available to players by default, and can only be unlocked by purchasing the Battlegrounds Season Pass , which costs real money or Runestones The most crucial reward granted by the Season Pass is the ability to select between 4 heroes at the start of a match, instead of just 2. This reward is granted immediately, at level 1. Other paid rewrads include boards , strikes, emotes, and hero skins of varying qualities. Since both the Free and Paid rewards use the same level progress, if the player is in the middle of a certain level, after purchasing the Season Pass, the player will be able to claim all previous levels' Paid rewards immediately. Runestones USD EUR 1500 $14.99 €14.99 Season Pass+ edit edit source The Season Pass+, added with Battlegrounds season 9 in Patch 31.2.0.212197 , is a version of the Season Pass that contains all the same rewards it has, but additionally makes the first hero reroll each game not consume a Battlegrounds Token The free reroll granted by Season Pass+ cannot be banked, and follows the same rules as regular rerolls. Contents Functionality Notes Buddies History 4.1 Buddy meter 4.2 Average results Speculations 5.1 Buddy Meter details Patch changes References Functionality edit edit source Unlike Tavern minions, Buddies do not appear in Bob's Tavern . Instead, every hero has a Buddy Button that has initial cost and can be activated twice per game. Initial cost is determined by Tavern Tier of the Buddy. The full details can be seen as below: Tavern Tier First cost Second cost 11 13 13 15 15 17 17 19 19 21 21 23 Winning a battle or getting Tie reduces this cost by (3), while losing only reduces by (2). The player clicks or taps the button to get the Buddies, as long as they have enough gold to spend. The first button gives the player one copy of their hero's Buddy, while the second and last button gives two copies. Notes edit edit source Buddy minions cannot be randomly generated. History edit edit source Buddy meter edit edit source Buddy meter From Patch 22.2.0.130051 to Patch 23.2.0.137922 , every hero used to have a Buddy Meter that fills up during the combat phase whenever the player accomplished one of these objectives: Enter combat The player also gets a small bonus for how many minions they have before entering Deal damage to enemies Pop Battlegrounds/Divine Shields Win or tie a combat phase Buddies were earned at three different rates. The lower Tavern Tier is, the quicker the player can get that Buddy There’s a limit to how much a Buddy Meter can be filled in a given round The Buddy Meter has two sections. The player fills the first section to get 1 copy of their hero’s Buddy added to their hand, and the second section to get 2 more copies. After both sections have been filled, the Buddy Meter breaks and is no longer available for the rest of the match (regardless of whether the player tripled their Buddy or sold any copies off along the way). The player can hover over heroes to see their buddy. The player can hover over the Buddy Meter to see the percentage. Buddy Meter details edit edit source As the Buddies were released along with Patch 22.2.0.130051 , a number of players have conducted researches to figure out how exactly Buddy Meters work and the metric system involved. At 1AM UTC, January 28, 2022, an user named u/moocowfan ( moocowalex on Twitch ) has published a post to share what they have found so far. Their research is regarded by the community to be one of the most detailed explanations to the Buddy Meter system. The post can be summarized as followed: Different Buddy Meter tiers have a "pool" of about 75, 100, and 125 points to get the first buddy in the first section, for Tavern Tier 2, 3, and 4 respectively (the numbers are arbitrary). The second section seems to take twice as many points compared to the first section. The percentage displayed on Buddy Meter is rounded down. For example, the player may have achieved 4.8%, but the visual display will show it as 4%. Each turn, Buddy Meter can gain only around 30% on the first section; and 25% for Tavern Tier 2 and 20% for Tavern Tier 3/4 on the second section (regarding to the limiting factor) Objectives Enter combat: The player gets percentage based on Tavern Tier of their Buddy and the turn. Deal damage to enemies: This includes the amount of damage Battlegrounds/Hero Powers or the player's minions deal to enemy minions. Tavern Tier of enemy minions, number of attacks, destroyed minions are not related. Dealing 1 damage 5 times and dealing 5 damage 1 time gives the same percentage. The amount of percentage the player gets from the damage decays turn after turn. The formula for calculating percentage seems to be , with as percentage per damage, and as turn. Pop Divine Shields: Popping Divine Shields consistently gives 0-2% of the meter depending on Buddy's Tavern Tier. Win or tie a combat phase: Tying gives roughly 1-3% Winning may give as high as 10% early game. Winning percentage may be increased based on the damage the player deals to enemy hero. Despite the existence of limit to how much percentage Buddy Meter can gain per turn, winning or tying will still give roughly 1-2%. Number of minions at start of combat: This bonus is very small and much less impactful than damage. If the scaling for damage is ~2.2% per damage for Tavern Tier 2 on turn 1, the percent per minion is something like 0.1-0.3%. Patch changes edit edit source Patch 29.6.0.201108 (2024-06-17): Added. UNMATCHED_Collection_manager.text: heroes in the collection Accessing the Battlegrounds collection from the Battlegrounds menu Clicking the "Show All" button allows both unlocked and locked heroes to be viewed. Clicking on a hero presents its hero power and flavor text. View of the player's bartenders View of the player's boards View of the player's strikes View of the player's emotes View of the Emote Deck For the regular collection manager used for constructed , see Collection manager The collection manager , also known as the collection , is where a player can go to view their Battlegrounds collection of heroes bartenders boards strikes , and emotes . It is accessed from the Battlegrounds menu by clicking the Collection button, found at the left side of the menu. Contents Functionality 1.1 Search Heroes Bartenders Boards Strikes Emotes Patch changes Functionality edit edit source As the Battlegrounds collection is not as in-depth as the constructed collection , its collection manager has fewer elements to it. Mainly, there is no crafting or decks (except for the deck-like visualization of the player's choice of emotes ), so the options for what the player can do in the collection manager are more limited. What sets the Battlegrounds collection manager apart from its constructed counterpart the most is that it is composed entirely of cosmetics . The available minions present during gameplay cannot be viewed in the collection. By default, only unlocked heroes are displayed, while unlocked and locked cosmetics for all other types are displayed at the same time. Search edit edit source A text search field at the bottom of the collection manager screen allows players to filter their collection, either by the item's name, or in some cases its description. Heroes and bartenders can be searched by name only; searching for the names of their hero powers or flavor text will yield no results. Other types of cosmetics can be searched for by their name or description. The following search functions are available in the Battlegrounds collection manager: Query Syntax Notes New new Lists only newly acquired cosmetics (those not yet moused over). Missing missing Lists only cosmetics the player does not own. Unlike the constructed collection manager, the Battlegrounds collection manager does not support the artist:<name> search function. Heroes edit edit source Main articles: Hero Hero skin The "Heroes" tab presents the player with their currently owned basic hero portraits and hero skins. Clicking on the "Show All" button on the top-right allows all heroes and skins to be viewed, regardless of whether they are locked or not. Clicking on a hero brings it up, showing a closer look at its artwork, as well as its Hero Power and flavor text. If a skin is not favorited, a "Make favorite" button will appear on the bottom of the screen, allowing that skin to be set as favorite. Favorited skins will be used in place of the default portrait of the hero whenever the player uses that hero in a match. Bartenders edit edit source Main article: Bartender The "Bartenders" tab presents the player with their currently owned and locked bartenders. Clicking on a bartender brings it up, showing a closer look at its artwork and a flavor text. Bartenders are fully voiced characters that can be favorited like hero skins, and they will appear in place of Bartender Bob during a match. Boards edit edit source Main article: Board The "Boards" tab presents the player with their currently owned and locked boards. Clicking on a board brings it up, showing a closer look at how it's presented during a game, as well as a description. Boards change the look of the battlefield during the Combat phase and the look of Bob's Tavern during the Recruit phase. Strikes edit edit source Main article: Strike The "Strikes" tab presents the player with their currently owned and locked strikes. Clicking on a strike brings it up, showing a video of how the strike performs during a match. Strikes are special attack animations during the Combat phase, that have two different forms depending on how much attack the Hero has. Emotes edit edit source Main article: Emote The "Emotes" tab presents the player with their currently owned and locked emotes. Clicking on an emote brings it up, showing a closer look as well as a description. Emotes are visualized versions of the regular emotes seen in constructed . Instead of a voiced paragraph, emotes in Battlegrounds are an animated image of a character. Like in constructed, heroes in Battlegrounds can have 6 selectable emotes. However, there is a special "Emote Deck" function in Battlegrounds, where the choice of emotes can be customized. Emotes can be dragged to the right side of the collection to the Emote Deck, and those emotes can be used during a match. The bottom-right also has a "Preview" button, where the player can view what their current Emote Deck will look like when viewed in-game. UNMATCHED_Emote.text: icon An emote in Battlegrounds Emotes are a type of cosmetic introduced in Patch 15.6.0.35747 . Players can use emotes by clicking on their Hero portrait, similarly to how emotes function in constructed Contents Functionality How to get Emotes 3.1 Free 3.2 Rare 3.3 Epic Functionality edit edit source View of the Emote Deck Everyone gets the "Starter Set" of 6 emotes as their default options. Battlegrounds Emotes are usable during the Recruit and Combat phases. Emotes in Battlegrounds are animated and feature a character, unlike their constructed counterparts that have voiced dialogue. The player can go to the Collection manager after navigating to the Battlegrounds window, click/tap on the speech bubble icon, and choose a set of 6 emotes to compose their Emote Deck, which can be used during gameplay. UNMATCHED_Hero.name: Hero
UNMATCHED_Hero.text: hero is a card type in Battlegrounds that the player controls. All heroes have health as the main resource to keep them alive. In Battlegrounds, most heroes start at 30 health. Each hero has their unique Hero Power with an unique cost and mechanics that the player can take account of to plan their strategy throughout the game. To win a Battlegrounds game, the player must deal damage to all other 7 heroes to reduce their health 0, while their hero must keep its health above 0 or end at top 4. Contents Notes Available heroes Special heroes History 4.1 Functionality 4.2 Removed heroes Patch changes Notes edit edit source If two or more heroes die at the same turn, whoever has less health after receiving damage will be placed lower. Heroes can only take a set amount of damage depending on the mode and game state: In regular Battlegrounds, if more than 4 heroes are still alive, heroes can take 5 damage at most until turn 4, then 10 damage at most until turn 8, then 15 damage at most after that. In Duos , heroes can only take 15 damage at most if more than 4 heroes are still alive. Each hero has a set Armor value from 5-20 (based on their power level) that adds to their maximum health. History edit edit source Functionality edit edit source Prior to Patch 25.6.0.168788 , each hero would gain a random amount of Armor based on their armor tier. This was replaced with set armor values for each hero. Removed heroes edit edit source These heroes were retired or removed , used to be available, or are temporarily banned. Patch changes edit edit source Patch 31.2.0.212197 (2024-12-03): Damage cap updated for regular Battlegrounds to start at 5 damage until turn 4, then 10 damage until turn 8, then 15 damage. Patch 27.4.0.185749 (2023-09-19): The damage cap now persists for all players until the Top 4, instead of until one player dies. Patch 25.6.0.168788 (2023-03-14): Starting health for heroes is now 30. Armor tiers removed: Heroes now have a set amount of armor instead, from 5 to 20. Patch 21.8.0.126299 (2021-11-16) Armor tiers added. Each hero now has a random amount of armor based on their armor tier. UNMATCHED_Hero_skin.name: Hero skin
UNMATCHED_Hero_skin.text: is a hero skin of Alexstrasza Collection manager icon Hero skins are a type of cosmetic in Battlegrounds introduced in Patch 21.0.0.88998 . They replace the appearance of the player's Hero Contents Functionality How to get Hero skins 3.1 Rare 3.2 Epic 3.3 Legendary Functionality edit edit source Every Hero has a default skin that is available to everyone. The player can go to the Collection manager and click/tap on the crown-like icon to view currently available heroes in Battlegrounds. On PC, there is a toggle to "Show All" that shows both the default skins and all other skins of heroes. The player can choose a hero to mark it as Favorite , which will then be used in-game whenever the player uses that hero. There are three main types of hero skins: Rare hero skins, marked with a purple border, have non-animated artworks and no voicelines. Epic hero skins, marked with a half-golden border, are animated but have no voicelines. Legendary hero skins, marked with a fully golden border, are animated and have voicelines. How to get edit edit source Hero skins can be available for obtaining in the following ways: Buying bundles in the Shop Buying individual skins in the Shop Claiming for free in the Shop Gaining levels in the Battlegrounds Track Hero skins edit edit source As of patch 35.2.2.241135 , there are a total of 575 hero skins in Battlegrounds. UNMATCHED_Quilboar.text: , the central card for Quilboar Quilboar is a minion type in Battlegrounds Quilboar minions' effects rely on Blood Gems , a spell that is exclusive to this minion type. When the player has Blood Gems, they can choose to play them immediately to give minions stats, or save them for later to either find a better minion to benefit from them, or use them on Quilboar minions that have direct synergies with Blood Gems. There are two main types of effects that may appear on minions in the Quilboar pool: Those that generate Blood Gems, and those that benefit from the player using Blood Gems on them. Quilboar in Battlegrounds are represented by the druid class border color. UNMATCHED_Tavern_Tier.name: Tavern Tier
UNMATCHED_Tavern_Tier.text: The Tavern Tier is an unique mechanic exclusive to Battlegrounds In Battlegrounds, instead of minions having a mana cost , they have a Tavern tier, typically ranging from 1 to 6 (with Tier 7 existing in special occasions). Minions can be purchased depending on which Tavern tier the player is currently at, and theTtavern tier itself can be upgraded for Gold Contents Functionality Related cards 2.1 Minions 2.2 Others References Functionality edit edit source Main article: Battlegrounds Upon entering the Tavern, Bob will have a group of minions lined up ready to be purchased. Minions can be purchased by dragging the minion over your hero or into your hand. Each minion costs 3 Coins (no matter their Tavern Tier), so choose wisely. Available minions automatically reset at the start of each round. You can access higher-tier minions by upgrading your Tavern Tier. The minions that are offered to you in Bob's Tavern come from a pool of shared minions, shared by all players. All minions that are at or below your Tavern Tier level are available to be offered to you in Bob's Tavern, with the minions being randomly selected from the shared pool. Because the minion pool is shared, if another player buys a minion that you can buy (and the player is also still alive), you will have less chance of being offered that specific minion when Bob's Tavern is re-rolled, because there is one less in the pool. At any time, you can upgrade your Tavern to the next tier. This will improve the quality of minions offered and occasionally increase the number of minions for sale. The number of minions offered to the player starts at 3 and is increased by 1 at tiers 2, 4 and 6. Taverns start at tier 1 and can be upgraded to tier 6. Your current Tavern Tier is displayed on a small flag next to Bob, and is visible to all players when they hover over. Upgrading will also notify every other player which tier you currently are. Upgrading starts at 5 Coins, and each upgrade costs more than the last. However, at the start of each round, the cost of upgrading reduces by 1. For non-Tavern spells generated by other cards in Battlegrounds, see Spell Tavern spell is an unique card type that only appears in Battlegrounds . They have a Tavern " spell school " listed on the bottom of the card, something all other spells in Battlegrounds lack. Like minions, Tavern spells have Tiers , and can only be found in the Tavern once that Tier has been reached. UNMATCHED_Timewarped_Tavern.name: Timewarped Tavern
UNMATCHED_Timewarped_Tavern.text: The Timewarped Tavern is a system in Battlegrounds that features an alternate version of the Recruit phase that allows players to buy special cards. The Timewarped Tavern appears twice per game, on turns 6 and 9. On each appearance, players can buy cards that aren't normally found in the tavern. Cards are purchased for Chronum instead of Gold in the Timewarped Tavern. Cards in the shop cost one or two Chronum, and any unspent Chronum disappears at the end of the turn. Contents Notes 1.1 Card-specific notes Cards Related cards Gallery Patch changes References Notes edit edit source A timewarped card. Note the inclusion of the Chronum cost under the Tier. Official sources list notes related to the functionality of the Timewarped Tavern: The player cannot Freeze or Refresh the Timewarped Tavern. The player's hand, board, and hero power do not function here. The player can buy any amount of cards in the Timewarped Tavern, even if their hand would get full. In any such case, the player's hand size will temporarily increase to hold all bought cards. Timewarped cards cannot triple with their regular versions, only with their timewarped versions. The Timewarped Tavern will always offer three cards that cost 1 Chronum and two cards that cost 2 or more Chronum. The Timewarped Tavern will always offer 3 minions and 2 non-minions (i.e. spells or hero powers). The Minor Timewarp will always offer a 2nd hero power as an option (unless the player already has 2 hero powers). Cards in the Timewarped Tavern are divided into two pools: Minor and Major. Minor Timewarped cards will appear on Turn 6 and will be Tier 3 cards. Major Timewarped cards will appear on Turn 9 and will be Tier 5 cards. Similar to Trinkets , the pool of eligible Timewarped cards they can be offered will be based on the minion types in the game, the player's warband, and their hero power. Some Timewarped cards have an internal tag that ties them to a particular type. In each offering, the player will get at least one card that has that type. Timewarped cards for the player's most common minion type will get offered more frequently. A Timewarped card can be considered part of a type even if the card doesn't have that minion type (e.g. Timewarped Nomi for Elementals Timewarped Whelp Smuggler for Dragons ). A Timewarped card can be considered NOT part of a type even if it has that minion type (e.g. Timewarped Lubber can be offered in lobbies without Elementals or Pirates ). The player needs 2 minions of a type to be considered "in" for the Minor Timewarp. For the Major Timewarp, they need 3 minions. Certain heroes can always be offered typed Timewarped cards even if they don't have minions of that type in their warband (e.g. Queen Azshara can be offered Naga ). Timewarped cards will be arranged by cost in the Tavern. The player needs 3 minions of different types to be considered "in" menagerie. The player cannot be offered more than 1 card from a type that isn't their most common type. The timewarped tavern uses Nozdormu as the bartender Card-specific notes edit edit source The player cannot be offered multiple Timewarped StarCraft cards. Timewarped Leapfrogger cannot be offered in Duos. N'Zoth cannot be offered Timewarped Saurolisk The player cannot be offered Timewarped Mothership Timewarped Geomancer , or Timewarped Recycler unless they have at least 4 minions. Trade Prince Gallywix Millhouse Manastorm Sindragosa Fungalmancer Flurgl Cap'n Hoggarr , and Kael'thas Sunstrider cannot be offered Timewarped Skipper The player cannot be offered Timewarped Lei if their hero doesn't have a Buddy The player cannot be offered Power of Al'Akir Power of George Power of Teron Power of Guff Power of Zephrys Power of Flurgl , or Power of Sylvanas if they already have their respective hero powers. The player cannot be offered Timewarped Jungle King Timewarped Tamuzo , or Timewarped Karathress if they did not summon any minions in the previous combat. The player cannot be offered Timewarped Whirl-O-Tron if they don't have a Deathrattle minion. The player cannot be offered Timewarped Murk-Eye if they don't have a Battlecry minion. The player cannot be offered Timewarped Sylvar if they have no Golden minions. The player cannot be offered Timewarped Stoneshell if they don't have a Rally minion. Special notes for Timewarped Thief This card is rarer than almost all other Timewarped cards The player cannot be offered Timewarped Thief if their past warband had 5 or less minions on it Timewarped Thief will generate cards from the player's last warband in the mode they're playing in. For example, if they play Timewarped Thief in Duos, it will offer based on their last Duos warband, not Solos. Timewarped Thief allows the player to get minions that don't exist in their current lobby (e.g. a Beast when Beast are not in their lobby) Timewarped Thief allows the player to get minions that have been removed from the pool since the player's last game, and thus are no longer in the game.
